title: ATR-normalized EMA20 trend-acceleration admission for DRA entries
thesis: An otherwise valid BTC DRA signal whose causally updated EMA20 remains above its five-day-ago value but has negative five-day slope acceleration may represent a decelerating trend approaching exhaustion; vetoing only that new entry may improve matched-capital realized and total PnL without changing the parent signal, exits or existing inventory.
mechanism: At the unchanged DRA signal and before its next-H1-open fill, preserve the parent capacity check first. For a capacity-admissible signal, compute ((EMA20[t]-EMA20[t-5])-(EMA20[t-5]-EMA20[t-10]))/ATR14[t] from complete UTC days after the signal day's indicators update. Admit at or above zero and veto below zero, reserving the unchanged seven-day cooldown from the original signal. Missing feature inputs veto fail-closed. Thresholds -0.10 and +0.10 ATR are rejection-only stability neighbors; lot cost remains 30 USDT, effective open-cost capacity 240 USDT and maximum open lots eight. Existing lots, the parent thirty-day arm lifecycle and the DRA V1 profit-only exit remain unchanged.
economic_rationale: The byte-identical pre-economic screen passed exact parent-path parity, action deduplication, feature availability, support, breadth, selectivity and concentration gates. The zero-curvature primary veto fired 40 of 100 capacity-admissible Design signals and 26 of 51 Validation signals, with 5 to 14 actions in every annual fold, top-year share 25 percent and Validation top-month share 15.384615 percent. This permits one matched-capital experiment but is not performance evidence. The mechanism succeeds only if excluding decelerating signals improves fee-adjusted Design and Validation realized and total PnL with acceptable unrealized, drawdown, underwater, holding, utilization, annual-breadth and terminal-inventory paths, while both frozen neighbors remain stable.
